source_refs.note: v. Dehydration of alcohols: a main subheading of 22.4 Reactions of Alcohols, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 92-95.

blocks.text: Alcohols can also undergo dehydration to form alkenes. Dehydration is the type of the elimination reaction in which a water molecule is removed.

blocks.alt: Displayed ETHANOL, with Al2O3 over the arrow and Heat under it, gives displayed ETHENE, H2C=CH2, + H2O.
blocks.caption: Dehydration of ethanol to ethene (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 94).

blocks.text: Dehydrating agents may be aluminium oxide, conc. sulphuric, acid, conc phosphoric acid, etc.
